coverage: The week of November 1-7, 2026 (Bible Loop public launch announced November 4, 2026)

feature.title: Bible Loop: YouVersion and OneHope build a Scripture app just for teens
feature.why: A free, purpose-built Bible app aimed at the age when Bible habits tend to slip. OneHope's research, quoted in the release, shows weekly engagement falling from 88% at ages 6-9 to 73% at ages 10-12. The app tries to build daily rhythms through verse memorization games, prayers, mood-matched devotional check-ins and lessons from partner ministries. Material new development versus the 2026-10-11 YouVersion topic, which covered search data, not this product. Editorial caveats: (1) the app appears to have been listed in stores before the official launch (faith.tools listing checked 2026-10-22), so describe November 4 as the official launch, not first availability; (2) a '1 million installs' headline (Christianity Daily) is unconfirmed by YouVersion and is based on third-party tracker counts, so do not state it as fact; (3) the release itself says Bible Loop was shaped for 'preteens' in one quote and 'teens' elsewhere, so describe the audience as young teens and preteens.

wisdomConcern: Gamifying Scripture for teens: a verse-memory game and leaderboard can build habits, but streaks and points can turn time with God into a score. Also, any app that collects profiles from minors needs clear parent-facing privacy and data disclosures (a reviewer flagged this; confirm against the app's own privacy policy before stating it). Parents and youth leaders should use the app as a doorway into the Bible and into real community, not as a substitute.
